translations.text: And God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.
And God called the dry land Earth, and he called the gathered waters Sea. And God saw that it was good.
And there was evening, and morning came, and it was the third day.
And God made two great lights: the greater light to rule the day, and the smaller light to rule the night, together with its stars.
And God placed them in the expanse of heaven to shine upon the earth.
And God said, “Let the water bring forth moving creatures that have the breath of life, and birds that fly above the earth and below heaven.” And it was so.
And God said, “Let the earth bring forth kinds of livestock, moving creatures, and wild animals of the earth, each according to its kind.” And it was so.
And every plant [of the field, before it existed on the earth, and every plant] of the earth, before it sprouted—for God had not sent rain upon the earth before a human being was created.
And God commanded Adam and said to him, “Eat from every tree that is in the garden.”
And God said, “It is not good for the man to live alone. Let us make him a companion who will help him.”
And Adam and his wife were naked, and they were not ashamed.
And God called Adam and said to him, “Where are you?”
“I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring. He shall watch your head, and you shall watch his heel.”
And Adam named his wife Eve, because she was the mother of the living.
And God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife and clothed them.
And the Lord God sent Adam out of the garden of delight to cultivate the earth from which he had come.
But he did not look upon Cain or his offering. This greatly distressed Cain, and he fell on his face.
And God said to Cain, “Where is Abel your brother?” And he said to him, “I do not know. Am I my brother’s keeper?”

And Adam had intercourse with Eve his wife, and she conceived and bore him a son. He named him Seth and said, “Look, now God has provided me with another offspring in place of Abel, whom Cain killed.”
And Seth also fathered a son and named him Enosh. Then he began to call upon the name of God.
And Adam lived 230 years and fathered a son in his own image and likeness, and named him Seth.
And Adam lived 700 years after fathering Seth, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And the whole span of Seth’s life was 912 years, and he died.
And Mahalalel lived 730 years after fathering Jared, and he fathered sons and daughters.
And the whole span of Enoch’s life was 365 years.
Enoch pleased God and was taken away, because God took him (into paradise).
All the days of Methuselah were 969 years, and he died.
[This is the account of Noah: he was a righteous man and blameless] in his generation, and he pleased God.
This is how you shall make the ark: 300 cubits long, [50] cubits wide, and 30 cubits high.
Noah did just as God, his God, commanded him; that is what he did.
Bring with you seven of each kind of clean animal, male and female, and two of each kind of unclean animal, male and female.
Of the clean birds of the sky, take seven of each kind, male and female, and of the unclean birds of the sky, two of each kind, male and female, to keep offspring alive on the earth.
The water grew very strong over the earth and increased, and the ark floated on the water.
The water increased exceedingly over the earth and covered all the high mountains under the sky.

Everything that moved on the face of the earth was wiped out, from human beings to animals, creeping creatures, and birds of the sky. They were wiped out from the earth. Only Noah remained, along with those who were with him in the ark.
After it, he sent out the dove to see whether the water had receded from the face of the earth.
The dove returned to him toward evening, with an olive leaf in its mouth, and Noah knew that the water had receded from the earth.
With every living creature that is with you—the birds, the animals, and all the wild animals of the earth that are with you, which came out of the ark.
I will set my bow in the clouds, and it will be a sign of my covenant between me and the whole earth.
The beginning of his kingdom was Babylon, [Erech], Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
And the Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites. After this, the Canaanites scattered.
Two sons were born to Eber. The name of one was Peleg, because in his days the earth was divided, and his brother's name was Joktan.
The whole world had one language and one form of speech.
When they journeyed from the east, they found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.
God said, “Look, they are all one people and have one language, and this is what they have begun to do. Now they will not stop doing what they have planned.”
“Come, let us go down and confuse their language, so that they will not understand one another's speech.”
After fathering Arphaxad, Shem lived 500 [years], had sons and daughters, and died.
After fathering Eber, he lived [3]30 years, had sons and daughters, and died.
[After fathering Nahor, Serug] lived 200 [years], had sons and daughters, and died.
I will bless those who bless you and curse those who curse you, and all the nations of the earth will be blessed because of you.
When the Egyptians see you, they will say, “She is his wife,” and they will kill me, but they will keep you alive.
The Lord afflicted Pharaoh and his household with great and terrible suffering because of Sarai, Abram’s wife.
The land could not support them living together.
For twelve years they were subject to Chedorlaomer (and the kings who were with him), but in the thirteenth year they rebelled.
After this, the word of the Lord came to Abram in a vision, and he said to him, “Do not be afraid, Abram. I will strengthen you, and your reward with me is very great.”
Then the word of the Lord came, saying, “This man will not be your heir. Another will come from you, and he will be your heir.”
They said to Abram, “Know for certain that your descendants will live as foreigners in a land that is not theirs. They will enslave them, afflict them, and oppress them for four hundred years.”
“But I will judge the nation that afflicts them, and afterward they will come out here with many possessions.”
“But you will go and be gathered to your ancestors at a good old age.”
On that day the Lord confirmed to Abram what he had promised him, saying, “To your descendants I will give this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the Euphrates.”

Sarai said to Abram in the land of Canaan, “Look, the Lord God has prevented me from bearing children. Go, then, and sleep with my slave woman, so that you may have children by her.” Abram listened to Sarai.
After Abram had lived in the land of Canaan for ten years, Sarai took Hagar, her Egyptian slave woman, and gave her to Abram to be his wife.
Abram said to Sarai his wife, “Your slave woman is in your hands. Do to her as you see fit.” Sarai mistreated Hagar, and she fled from her.
The angel of the Lord said to her, “Return to your mistress and humble yourself under her authority.”
Abram was eighty-seven years old when Hagar bore Ishmael to him.
“My ordinance in your flesh will be my everlasting covenant.”
“For I will bless her and give her children by you; nations and kings of nations will come from her.”
Abraham was ninety-nine years old at the time when the foreskin of his flesh was circumcised.
When he lifted his eyes and looked, there were three men standing over him. When he saw them, he ran from the entrance of the tent to meet them and bowed down to the ground.
“Let us bring water and wash your feet, and you can rest in the shade under the tree.”
Sarah denied it, saying, “I did not laugh,” because she was afraid. But he said to her, “No, you did laugh.”
Those (two) men rose from there and looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah. Abraham went with them to see them on their way.
Abraham answered and said, “Now I have undertaken to speak with my Lord God, though I am earth and dust.”
Abraham said to him, “What if forty are found there?” The Lord said to him, “I will not destroy it for the sake of the forty.”

He said to them, “My lords, turn aside to your servant’s house, spend the night, and wash your feet. Then you can rise early and go on your way.” They said to him, “No, we will spend the night in the square.”
Lot went out to them at the doorway and shut the door behind him.
They said to him, “Get away! You came here to stay, not to judge us. Now we will mistreat you more than those men.” They pressed hard against the man and came forward to break down the door.
Those men took hold of his hand, his wife’s hands, and those of his two daughters, because the Lord had mercy on them.
“For I have found mercy in your sight, and you have shown me great mercy by keeping me alive. But I cannot escape to the mountain, lest disaster overtake me and I die.”
“Hurry, then, and escape there.” For this reason that town was named Zoar.
The Lord rained fire and sulfur upon Sodom and Gomorrah, from the Lord out of heaven.
He looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah and all the surrounding land. As he looked, there was smoke rising from the earth like the smoke of a furnace.
When he destroyed all the towns and all the surrounding land, God remembered Abraham and brought Lot out of the midst of the destruction, when God destroyed those towns in which he lived.
Lot went up from Zoar and fled to the mountain, with his two daughters, because he was afraid to live in Zoar. He lived in a cave, he and his two daughters.
“When God brought me out of my father’s house, I said, ‘Show me this kindness: wherever we go, say, “He is my brother.”’”
Then, in the wilderness of Paran, his mother took a wife for him from the land of Egypt.
Abimelech said to Abraham, “What are these seven sheep that you have set apart by themselves?”
Abraham said to him, “Accept these seven sheep from me, so that they may be a witness for me that I dug this well.”
Abraham planted a field at the Well of the Oath, and there Abraham called upon the name of the everlasting Lord.
After these days, God tested Abraham and said to him, “Abraham, Abraham!” He said, “Here I am.”
He said to him, “Take your son whom you love, your Isaac, and go to the high mountain. Bring him up to me and sacrifice him on one of the mountains that I will tell you about.”
Abraham said to the young men, “Stay here with the donkey. My son and I will go over there, and after we have worshiped, we will return to you.”
Isaac said to Abraham his father, “Father!” He said to him, “What is it, my son?” He said to him, “Here are the wood and the fire, but where is the sheep for the sacrifice?”
Ephron was sitting among the descendants of Heth. Ephron the Hittite spoke to Abraham in the hearing of the descendants of Heth and everyone entering the town:
He said to Ephron in everyone’s hearing, “Since you are close to me, listen to me. Accept the price of that field from me, and I will bury my dead there.”
Ephron’s field, its cave, and all the trees within it became his.
Abraham said to his eldest son, who managed all his possessions, “Put your hand upon my hand.”
“But if the woman is unwilling to come with you to this land, you are free from the oath. Only take care not to bring my son back there.”

“Let it be the virgin to whom I say, ‘Lower your jar so that I may drink water,’ and who says to me, ‘Drink, and I will also give your camels water until they have had enough.’ Let her be the one you have prepared for your servant Isaac. By this I will know that you have shown mercy to my master Abraham.”
She quickly emptied her jar into the drinking trough, then ran and drew water for all his camels.
The man watched her [?] and remained silent to see whether the Lord would make his journey successful or not.

My master said to me, “The Lord God, whom I have pleased, will send his angel ahead of you and make your journey successful. You will take a wife for my son from there, (and if not [?]) from my clan, and [?] in my father’s household.”
“Here is Rebekah. Take her and go, and let her become the wife of your master’s son, as the Lord has said.”
He told Isaac, his son, everything he had done.
Isaac entered his mother’s house, and then he took Rebekah, and she became his wife. He loved her, and Isaac’s grief over his mother was soothed.
This was Abraham’s lifespan: his years were one hundred and seventy-five years.
This is the genealogy of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, whom Hagar, Sarah’s servant, bore to him.
He lived alone from Havilah to Shur, which is in Egypt, and reached as far as Assyria. He lived opposite all his brothers.
Her children struggled together in her womb, and she said, “If this is how it is for me, why is this happening to me?” She went to inquire of the Lord God.
Esau said to Jacob, “Give me some of your cooked food to eat, because I am very tired.” Because of this, he was named Edom.
The Lord God appeared to him and said, “Do not go down to Egypt. Stay in the land that I tell you.”
He commanded all his people, saying to them, “Anyone who harms this man will be sentenced to a terrible death.”

Isaac again dug the wells of water that the servants of his father Abraham had dug, which the Philistines had filled in after his father Abraham died. He gave them the names that Abraham had given them.
He moved from there to Beersheba.
They said to him, “When we saw that the Lord God was with you, we said, ‘Let there be an oath between you and us, and let us swear to one another.’”
They rose in the morning and swore oaths to one another. Isaac sent them away, and they went in peace.
He said to him, “Look, I have grown old, and I do not know the day of my death.”
“My father might feel me, and I would seem to him like someone mocking him. I would bring a curse upon myself, not a blessing.”
He went and brought it to his mother, and she prepared food for his father just as he liked it.
Rebekah took the fine clothes of her older son Esau, which she had with her, and dressed her younger son Jacob in them.
She also put the skins of the two young goats on his arms and neck.
He went in to his father and said, “Father!” His father said to him, “Here I am. Who are you, my son?”
Jacob said to him, “I am Esau, your firstborn. I have done what you told me. Get up, sit down, and eat some of what I have hunted for you, so that your soul may bless me.”
Isaac said to his son, “How did you find it so quickly, my son?” He said to him, “The Lord your God put it before me.”
Isaac said to him, “Come close and kiss me, my son.”
May nations serve you, and may angels bow down to you. Be lord over your brother, and may your father's sons bow down to you. May whoever blesses you be blessed, and whoever curses you be cursed.
Arise and go to Mesopotamia, to the house of Bethuel, your mother's father, and take a wife for yourself from the daughters of Laban, your mother's brother.
When Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan were displeasing to his father Isaac,
And bring me back safely to my father's house, and the Lord will be my God.
He looked and saw a well in the open country, and there were three sheep resting beside it, for they watered the sheep from that well. A large stone lay over the mouth of the well.
He gave Bilhah to Rachel to be her maidservant.
When the Lord saw that Leah was hated, he opened her womb, but Rachel was barren.
She conceived again and bore a son, and said, “Now, once again, I will give thanks to the Lord God for this.” Therefore she named him Judah. And she stopped bearing children.
Rachel said, “God has given judgment in my favor, heard my voice, and given me a son.” Therefore she named him Dan.

Jacob came in from the field toward evening, and Leah met him (toward evening) and said to him, “You will spend the night with me today, for I have bought you with my son's mandrakes.” And he spent that night with her.
When Rachel had given birth to Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, “Send me away so that I may go to my homeland and my own country.”
For I found them few in number, but they have increased and multiplied, and the Lord has blessed them wherever I have set foot. And now, when will I provide a household for myself?
Then, at the times when the sheep conceived, Jacob would place those rods before the sheep in the troughs, so that they would conceive while looking at those rods.
He said to them, “Look, I see from your father's face that he is not disposed toward me as he was before, but the God of my father is with me.”
All the wealth that God has taken from our father's house belongs to us and our children. Now do everything that God has told you.
Laban said to Jacob, “What have I done in secret, that you should wrong me and steal my daughters away like captives taken in war?”

Now look to see whether any of your belongings are with me, and take them. Laban went in but found nothing at all. Jacob said, “Whoever you find your gods with shall not live. Here, in the presence of these relatives of ours.” Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen them.
Jacob offered a sacrifice on the mountain and called his relatives. They ate and drank and spent the night on that mountain.
He spent that night there and brought out a gift to be taken to his brother Esau.
Tell him, “It belongs to your servant Jacob. It is a gift he has sent to his lord Esau, and he himself is following behind us.”
He said to him, “What is your name?” He answered, “Jacob.”
Jacob named that place “Vision of God,” for he said, “I have seen God face to face, and my life has been saved (and my face).”
He placed his concubines with their children in front, Leah and her children behind them, and Rachel with Joseph behind her.
Jacob heard that the son of Hamor had defiled his daughter Dinah. His sons were in the field with the livestock, and Jacob kept silent until they arrived.
Only on this condition will you become like us and we live with you: if you circumcise all your males.

Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “You have brought trouble on me and made me hated by everyone living throughout the land, among the Canaanites and Perizzites. I am few in number, and they will gather against me and kill me. I and my household will be destroyed.”
God appeared to Jacob when he came out of Mesopotamia in Syria, and God blessed him.
Then, as her life was about to leave her—for she was dying—she named him “Son of my suffering,” but his father named him Benjamin.
Isaac lived for one hundred and eighty years.
For their possessions were numerous, and they could not live together because of their many possessions.
These are the children of Anah: Dishon and Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah.
When Reuben saw him, he rescued him from their hands and said to them, “Do not take his life.”
He returned to his brothers and said to them, “The boy is not in the pit! Where am I to go now?”
They took it to their father and said to him, “We found this (blood). Look and see whether it is your son’s garment or not.”
He recognized it and said, “It is my son’s garment. A wild beast has eaten him; a beast has torn Joseph apart.”
Judah said to Onan, “Go in to your brother’s wife, fulfill your duty as her brother-in-law, and raise up offspring for your brother.”
Onan knew that the offspring would not be his. Whenever he went in to his brother’s wife, he spilled his semen on the ground so that he would not give offspring to his brother.
He too was evil in the Lord’s sight because he did this, and the Lord killed him too.
They informed Tamar, their daughter-in-law, saying to her, “Look, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep.”
After him, his brother also came out, the one who had [?] on his hand, and she named him Zerah.
When she saw that he had gone out and left his garment in her hand,
“When he heard that I raised my voice and cried out, he left his garment and fled outside.”
she kept his garment with her until his master came home.
“When he heard that I raised my voice and cried out, he left his garment and fled outside.”
Seven cows came up out of the river, from the riverbank, fat in body and beautiful in appearance, and they grazed in the meadow.
Those lean cows swallowed those seven fat and beautiful cows.
Joseph said to Pharaoh, “Pharaoh’s dream is one. God has shown Pharaoh what he is going to do.”
“Let Pharaoh build storehouses throughout the land of Egypt, and let them seal up Egypt’s grain from the seven years.”
Before the days of famine came, two sons were born to Joseph, whom Asenath bore to him.
There was famine throughout the land of Egypt, and all the people cried out to Pharaoh for food. He said to them, “Go to Joseph and do whatever he tells you.”
He said to them, “No! You are spies, and you have come to discover the unprotected parts of the land.”
But if you are honest, let one of you remain in prison, while the rest of you go and take the grain you have bought.

And they said to one another, “Truly, this has happened to us because of our sin, for we ignored our brother’s suffering when he pleaded with us for mercy, and we did not listen to him then. That is why this suffering has come upon us.”
And [?] answered them and said, “Did I not tell you, ‘Do not wrong the boy’? But you did not listen to me. Now, today, you are being called to account for his blood.”
After this, the famine became severe in the land.
And Israel said to them, “Why have you done this evil to me by telling that man that you have another brother?”
And the man did as Joseph told him and brought the men into Joseph’s house.
And they said to him, “Please, my lord, we came down before to buy grain.”
And they prepared their gift for Joseph’s arrival at noon, for they had heard that he would eat there.
And they said to him, “Your servant, our elderly father, is well, and he is still alive.” And Joseph said, “That man is blessed by God.” And they lowered their heads and bowed down to him.
And they received their portions from him, each his own. Benjamin’s portion was five times greater than any of theirs. And they drank and became drunk with him.
[And they entered Joseph’s house] while he was still [there], and they fell facedown on the ground.
And Joseph said to them, “What is this you have done?”
But you said to your servants, “Unless you bring your younger brother, you will not see my face again.”
And when we went up to your servant, our father, we told him what you had said to us, my lord.
And your servant, our father, said to us, “You yourselves know that this woman bore me two sons.”
“One went away from me, and you told me, ‘A wild animal ate him.’ And I have [?] seen him again to this day.”
“And now, if we go to your servant, our father, and this boy is not with us—for his life is bound to this boy—
as soon as he sees that the boy is not with us, he will die, and we will bring the gray hair of your servant, our father, down to the grave in anguish.”
And Joseph said to his brothers, “Come close to me.” And they came close to him. And Joseph said to them, “I am your brother Joseph, whom you sold into the land of Egypt.”
“And God sent me ahead of you so that you might live and survive on the earth, and so that I might provide for you.”
And the news was heard in Pharaoh’s house: “Joseph’s brothers have come.” And Pharaoh and all his people rejoiced.
“Let them not be concerned about their belongings or what their eyes behold, for all the bounty of Egypt belongs to them.”
And likewise for his father: he sent ten donkeys carrying some of all the bounty of Egypt, and ten mules carrying provisions for his father’s journey.
And the sons of Rachel, Jacob’s wife, were Joseph and Benjamin.

And children were born to Joseph in the land of Egypt: Manasseh and Ephraim. And the son of Manasseh whom his Syrian concubine bore him was [Machir, and Machir fathered Gilead]. And the sons of Ephraim, Manasseh’s brother, were [Shuthelah and Tahan, and the son of Shuthelah was Eden].
The sons of Benjamin were Bela, Becher, and Ashbel. These were the sons of Bela: Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, and Muppim. Gera fathered Ard.
All the people who entered the land of Egypt with Jacob, excluding the wives, numbered sixty-six.
Joseph prepared his chariots and went to meet his father Jacob in the city of Heroonpolis. When he met him, he embraced him around the neck and wept bitterly.
Israel said to Joseph, “Now let me die, since I have seen your face and you are alive.”

Jacob said to Pharaoh, “The years of my life that I have lived are one hundred and thirty. The days and years of my life have been few and miserable, and they have been as nothing compared with the days that my fathers lived.”
Joseph measured out wheat as food for his father, his brothers, and his father's entire household. He measured out a ration of wheat for each person.

All the gold in the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan was exhausted. All the people of Egypt came to Joseph and said to him, “Give us food so that we do not die before you, for our gold is exhausted.”
They brought their livestock to Joseph, and he gave them food in exchange for their sheep and cattle. In exchange for their donkeys, too, he supplied them with food that year.
They said to him, “You have kept us alive, and we have found favor in the sight of our lord. We will be Pharaoh's slaves.”
“But let me sleep with my fathers. Take me out of the land of Egypt and bury me in my fathers' burial place.” Joseph said to him, “Yes, I will do as you have said.”
They told Israel, “Look, your son Joseph is coming to you.” Israel gathered his strength and sat up on his bed.
Israel stretched out his right hand and placed it on Ephraim's head, though he was younger than his brother. He placed his left hand on Manasseh's head, crossing his hands.
He blessed them and said, “The God whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac pleased in his presence, the God who has cared for me and fed me from my youth until now, to this very day—
“Look, I give you fine spoil, better than your brothers' share, which I took from the hands of the Amorites with my bow and my spear.”
Naphtali is a plant of rest that produces beautiful fruit.
Those who attacked him with their schemes became his adversaries and struck him.

The blessing of your father and mother is stronger than the blessing of the mountains that are beloved through the blessing of God's angels. May it rest on Joseph's head and on the heads of those who became his brothers.
His sons brought him back to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave that Abraham had bought as a burial place from Ephron the Hittite, opposite Mamre.
Joseph saw Ephraim's descendants to the third generation, and the children of Machir, Manasseh's son, who were born on Joseph's lap.
